verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission launched on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Launch date April 1, 2026, 22:35:12 UTC (6:35:12 p.m. EDT); Artemis II lifts off from Launch Complex 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida on April 1, 2026
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the exact launch date and time.

verifications.claim: NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket is 322 feet tall.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: the 322-foot-tall rocket, weighing 5.75 million pounds
verifications.reasoning: R8 directly states the SLS rocket height as 322 feet.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission utilizes NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket to propel four astronauts around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: launched aboard an SLS rocket; Artemis II (April 1–11, 2026) was a crewed lunar flyby mission... carrying a crew of four astronauts
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm SLS used for Artemis II with four astronauts on lunar flyby trajectory.

verifications.claim: The Space Launch System (SLS) is the most powerful operational rocket.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.evidence: No relevant content found
verifications.reasoning: No source explicitly states SLS as the 'most powerful operational rocket'.

verifications.claim: The Space Launch System (SLS) generates over 8 million pounds of thrust.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: generated an incredible 8.8 million pounds of force at liftoff
verifications.reasoning: R6 confirms SLS generates 8.8 million pounds of thrust, over 8 million.

verifications.claim: The Space Launch System (SLS) sends the Orion capsule on a 10-day test flight.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: approximately ten-day trip; 10-day mission
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe Artemis II as a ~10-day test flight using SLS/Orion.

verifications.claim: The Space Launch System (SLS) produces more than 8 million pounds of thrust at liftoff.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: generated an incredible 8.8 million pounds of force at liftoff
verifications.reasoning: Direct match to thrust at liftoff exceeding 8 million pounds.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight to test SLS and Orion systems in deep space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: the second flight of the Space Launch System (SLS) and the first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft... first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17
verifications.reasoning: R1 confirms first crewed SLS/Orion in deep space.

verifications.claim: Artemis II performs a free-return trajectory around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: free-return trajectory around the Moon; slingshot “free return ” trajectory
verifications.reasoning: Multiple direct confirmations of free-return trajectory.

verifications.claim: The launch vehicle for Artemis II is the Space Launch System (SLS) Block 1.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Space Launch System (SLS) Block 1B rocket... but actual mission uses SLS Block 1 configuration with ICPS
verifications.reasoning: R1 details SLS Block 1 for Artemis II (early Block 1B planning revised).

verifications.claim: The Space Launch System (SLS) Block 1 consists of two solid rocket boosters and four RS-25 engines.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: two solid rocket boosters... The four RS-25 main engines; twin solid rocket boosters
verifications.reasoning: Standard SLS Block 1 configuration confirmed.

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II includes NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover... mission specialist Christina Koch
verifications.reasoning: All sources list these exact NASA astronauts.

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II includes CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: mission specialist Jeremy Hansen from the Canadian Astronaut Corps
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation across sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis II launched from Kennedy Space Center Complex 39B in Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Kennedy, LC-39B; lifted off from Kennedy Space Center Complex 39B
verifications.reasoning: Exact location confirmed.

verifications.claim: Artemis II carries the crew into a high Earth orbit before initiating a lunar flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: first day of the mission was spent largely in high Earth orbit... then traveled toward the Moon on a free-return trajectory
verifications.reasoning: R1 details high Earth orbit phase before lunar trajectory.

verifications.claim: The SLS lifts off using two solid boosters.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: the solid rocket boosters... ignited at T-0; twin solid rocket boosters
verifications.reasoning: Direct description of liftoff with two boosters.

verifications.claim: The two solid boosters provide over 75% of the initial power.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: delivering more than 75% of the thrust needed to lift the 5.75-million-pound rocket off the pad
verifications.reasoning: Exact percentage confirmed for initial thrust.

verifications.claim: The solid boosters separate from the core stage shortly after launch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Booster separation occurred at roughly 3,100 miles per hour... about six minutes after launch
verifications.reasoning: Separation shortly after launch confirmed.

verifications.claim: The main core stage separates.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The core stage burned for about eight minutes before separation; core stage separates from interim cryogenic propulsion stage
verifications.reasoning: Core stage separation explicitly described.

verifications.claim: The Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) maneuvers the Orion capsule toward the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: ICPS burn raised the perigee... to prepare for a trans-lunar injection (TLI) burn
verifications.reasoning: ICPS performs burns to set up lunar trajectory.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule separates from the rocket's upper stage once in space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Orion and ESM separated from the upper stage; spacecraft separates from the upper stage
verifications.reasoning: Separation after ascent confirmed.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II rocket features a mix of new and historically used hardware.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The four RS-25 engines (serial numbers E2047, E2059, E2062, and E2063) were installed... previously flew on shuttle missions
verifications.reasoning: RS-25 engines reused from Shuttle, mix of new/old hardware.

verifications.claim: The four RS-25 engines of the Artemis II rocket were previously used on several Space Shuttle missions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The four RS-25 engines... Engine E2047... flew on 15 space shuttle missions; E2059 on five
verifications.reasoning: Specific engines and their Shuttle flight history detailed.

verifications.claim: Artemis II serves as the final test before future Artemis missions land astronauts on the lunar surface.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: test flight supporting subsequent Artemis missions aimed at returning humans to the lunar surface
verifications.reasoning: Described as test ahead of landing missions, but not explicitly 'final test'.
